linkedin.title: This Week in Finance & Tech
linkedin.body:
The tech world has been busy this week, particularly with OpenAI. The company is removing rate limits for free ChatGPT users, meaning you will soon have unlimited access to text chats. On the hardware front, reports suggest their upcoming AI device will be a smart speaker priced between $300 and $400. Meanwhile, OpenAI is pushing back in its trade secrets case against Apple, arguing that Apple's own security practices weaken their claims.

In financial news, President Donald Trump is renewing his attempt to remove Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook. This move is part of a broader strategy to reshape the central bank's board.

Elsewhere, Google Wallet is rolling out a feature that lets parents set up secure balances for their children, aimed at helping kids learn financial management with built-in safeguards. In the UK, Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced new powers for councils to restrict the number of vape and betting shops in town centres, citing concerns over the decline of local high streets.

Looking at the broader markets, U.S. stock futures are holding steady as investors wait for upcoming inflation data. There is also ongoing caution regarding the Middle East, as Prime Minister Burnham warned that the conflict could impact UK economic growth due to rising energy costs and supply chain disruptions.

slides.headline: Twitch Users Push Back on AI Training
slides.explanation: Twitch is facing backlash after defaulting users into an agreement that lets Amazon use their streaming data to train AI models. This matters because it highlights growing concerns about how our personal content is being used without clear, active consent.

slides.headline: Private Firms to Lead Cyberattacks
slides.explanation: The Trump administration is starting a program that allows private companies to conduct cyberattacks against foreign criminals under government supervision. This shift could change how international cyber warfare is handled by bringing private sector speed into government operations.

slides.headline: OpenAI Unveils Ultrafast Model Mode
slides.explanation: OpenAI is testing a new mode for its latest model that runs 14 times faster than before. The company hopes this speed boost will attract more business clients who need AI to handle enterprise tasks quickly.

slides.headline: Bumble Drops Women-First Rule
slides.explanation: Bumble is removing its signature rule that required women to send the first message in heterosexual matches. The app says it made the change after testing showed users wanted more flexibility in how they start conversations.

slides.headline: Surveillance Firm Addresses Police Abuse
slides.explanation: The CEO of Flock admitted the company was too slow to act after police officers used their license plate cameras to stalk romantic partners. This raises serious questions about how surveillance technology is monitored and secured against misuse.
